answer: Picture each agent docking at a jetty where entry demands a proof-of-work puzzle whose difficulty auto-ratchets with the recent registration rate. One honest newcomer pays baseline compute, but a sybil flood spiking that thread of sign-ups triggers exponentially harder puzzles, so minting ten thousand fakes becomes ruinously expensive. The adaptive-difficulty atlas maps join-velocity to cost, pricing out swarms while leaving a lone agent barely taxed.
